reason: Quotes exist and WAGR-22 is an empty epic, but 'admin never named' is overstated: Eric was named on 3 Jun as the in-house person to ride along and own the org (L0144/L0164), got access in July (L0897), and the kickoff discussion refers to a specific 'him'. Handoff work also exists outside Jira (admin user manual L1709, 11 Aug; written handover doc L2183, 31 Aug). What remains: no formal confirmation of the admin, no handoff plan or date, and nothing tracked in Jira.
q1: Found. L0378 (doc 1A44vvYC..., lines 722/727/738 of the fetched text): all three lines are verbatim. 'That's totally fair.' is the start of a longer line, 'That's totally fair. For sure. ...', about 10 lines later. L0164 (doc 1CiCF1Km..., line 562): verbatim, an excerpt of a long line. L0145 (line 391/393): verbatim, with filler and words removed between the two pieces ('Um and he should work towards becoming a a Salesforce administrator...'). This is acceptable.
q2: Partly supports the claim. At kickoff Joyce said 'we're still talking internally about like who exactly', and that the admin would join after discovery. Emily and Joyce then talk about a specific 'him' ('he's a developer and a rep', 'he does things in a certain way'). This points to a known person (likely Eric) who was kept out of discovery on purpose. It does not show that there was no candidate. On 3 Jun Joyce named Eric as the in-house junior developer who would ride along, and Waleed said 'Eric is going to own it'. So the admin candidate was named. What is not confirmed is the formal admin role and the handoff plan. The Trailhead advice (L0145) was a Jumpr recommendation only.
q3: No later meeting formally names the WagerTech admin or sets a handoff date. Later items reduce the gap: L0205 (11 Jun), the client hopes its IT person becomes admin; L0896/L0897 (8 Jul), Eric gets access and takes part in testing; L1709 (11 Aug, tier2 decided), Kobi asked Taryn to start an admin user manual (user management and permission sets); L2183 (31 Aug, tier2 decided), a written handover document instead of video; L1707, a living user-facing training manual. These show that handoff documentation started but is not tracked in Jira. The claim 'no later meeting plans the handoff' is partly wrong.
q4: WAGR-22 live: Epic, Open, unassigned, 0 comments, no description, due 2026-08-14 (past due), Phase 1. JQL 'parent = WAGR-22 OR "Epic Link" = WAGR-22' returns 0 issues. The Asana Epic field cf[10227] = 'Training & Handoff' returns only WAGR-22. Text searches for 'admin manual', 'handoff', 'handover', 'training', 'administrator', 'Eric', 'Trailhead' and 'user manual' found no ticket for naming the client admin, the admin manual or the handover document. WAGR-449 'Access and Permissions' (Open) is related to permission-set content but is not a handoff ticket. Jira does not cover this.
corrections: Title overstates the gap: the candidate admin (Eric, junior developer) was named on 2026-06-03 (L0144, L0164) and was given sandbox access on 2026-07-08 (L0897). The gap is no formal confirmation of the admin role and no handoff plan, not an unnamed person.
Add later evidence: L1709 (2026-08-11) admin user manual started; L2183 (2026-08-31) written handover document; L1707 user-facing training manual. All are untracked in WAGR-22.
WAGR-22 due date 2026-08-14 has passed with no child tickets.
